classification.difficultyReason: Combine Pythagorean equations for three related triangles to prove a symbolic altitude relationship.

content.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse $c$ divides the hypotenuse into two line segments of lengths $p$ and $q$. If we denote the length of the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse by $h$, then prove that $h=\sqrt{pq}$.

spec.description: Right triangle with vertical leg a, horizontal leg b and an altitude to the sloping hypotenuse, divided into p and q. Both right-angle marks retained; decorative cyan fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: The altitude endpoint is the orthogonal projection of the right-angle vertex onto the hypotenuse. Coordinates specify drawing geometry only, with no numerical labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Neither h nor c is added to the diagram; both remain defined in the source stem.

answer.short:
$h=\sqrt{pq}$.

Apply Pythagoras to the whole triangle and both smaller triangles, then cancel $p^2+q^2$.
answer.worked:
For the two smaller right triangles,
$$\begin{align*}a^2&=p^2+h^2\\b^2&=q^2+h^2\end{align*}$$
For the whole triangle,
$$\begin{align*}(p+q)^2&=a^2+b^2\\p^2+2pq+q^2&=(p^2+h^2)+(q^2+h^2)\\2pq&=2h^2\\h^2&=pq\\h&=\sqrt{pq}\end{align*}$$
Take the positive root because $h$ is a length.
